title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Addresses Mahaparva Kshamapana Ceremony in New Delhi
subtitle:
“Forgiveness Means Choosing Reform Over Revenge, Dialogue Over Hatred and Reconciliation Over Hostility”: Vice-President

“Ahimsa Means Absence of Violence in Thought, Word and Deed”: Vice-President

“A Truly Developed India Must Have Trust Among Citizens, Values in Families, Character Among Youth and Compassion in Society”: Vice-President

“Jain Philosophy of Friendship with All Living Beings and Enmity Towards None Can Guide a Peaceful World Order”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the Mahaparva Kshamapana Ceremony – 2026, organised by the Bhagwan Mahavir Memorial Committee and Jain Mahasabha Delhi at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. He described the occasion as a celebration of universal values of forgiveness, friendship, non-violence and inner purification.
Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Mahaparva Kshamapana Ceremony-2026 in New Delhi, highlighting the timeless Jain values of forgiveness, Ahimsa, friendship and compassion. 

He said forgiveness means choosing reform over revenge, dialogue over hatred and reconciliation over hostility, while Ahimsa means absence of violence in thought, word and deed.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 4, 2026
The Vice-President said that the depth with which the Jain tradition has transformed forgiveness into a spiritual discipline holds profound relevance for India and humanity today. He underlined that Kshamapana is not merely a ritual, but an opportunity for transformation of the human heart.
Highlighting the deep historical connection between Tamil Nadu and Jainism, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Jainism has made significant contributions to Tamil literature and culture. He recalled the contributions of Jain scholars and monks to classical Tamil literature and noted the presence of ancient Jain temples and centres of learning across Tamil Nadu.
Emphasising the universal message of Jain philosophy, the Vice-President said the teaching of friendship towards all living beings and enmity towards none resonates with India’s civilisational ethos of “Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam”. In a world witnessing conflict and violence, he said, the teachings of Bhagwan Mahavira offer a path towards peace, dialogue, coexistence and compassion.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said Ahimsa is not merely the absence of physical violence, but also the absence of violence in thought, word and deed. He said Bhagwan Mahavira showed humanity the path of inner victory, reminding people that true strength lies in conquering anger, intolerance and revenge.
On Kshamapana, the Vice-President said forgiveness does not mean accepting injustice or compromising with truth. “Forgiveness means choosing reform over revenge, dialogue over hatred and reconciliation over hostility,” he said, adding that the spirit of Pratikraman can help individuals and families acknowledge mistakes and resolve conflicts.
Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said development must go beyond economic prosperity, modern infrastructure and technological advancement. A truly developed India, he said, must also have trust among citizens, values within families, character among youth and compassion in society, in keeping with the vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi.”
The Vice-President called upon people to nurture the values of humility, compassion, service, unity and responsibility while building a developed India. On the occasion, he also presented the Jain Samaj Ratna Award to Shri K. C. Jain. Those present included Governor of Punjab Shri Gulab Chand Kataria; President, Bhagwan Mahavir Memorial Committee, Shri Kanhaiya Lal Jain; President, Jain Mahasabha Delhi, Shri Dinesh Doshi; Acharya Shri Visuddh Sagarji Muniraj; Shri Vipin Jain, General Secretary, Shree Jain Tarun Samaj Bhagwan Mahaveer Memorial Samiti; Munishri Udit Kumar Ji; Munishri Tirth Nirvaan Vijay Ji; and Upadhyay Shri Ravinder Muni Ji.

date:

content:
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today addressed the 58th Foundation Day celebrations of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Extending his greetings to the entire ICSI fraternity, he commended the Institute for its nearly six-decade journey in strengthening transparent, ethical and inclusive corporate governance.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graced the 58th Foundation Day celebrations of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI) at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. 

He emphasised that good governance is the “invisible infrastructure” that sustains investor confidence and public trust, and described Company Secretaries as the “Guardians of Governance” and the nucleus of India Inc.’s trust architecture.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 4, 2026
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the transformation of the Institute mirrors the evolution of the profession, which today has an important role in strengthening corporate transparency, investor confidence and India’s standing in the global economy.
In an era shaped by Artificial Intelligence, advanced data analytics and rapidly evolving business models, the Vice-President called upon Company Secretaries, as “Guardians of Governance,” to uphold the legal, strategic and ethical foundations of India Inc. “Technology may transform the manner in which information is generated and decisions are supported, but integrity, accountability, transparency and responsibility remain human,” he said.
Describing trust, transparency and corporate governance as the “invisible infrastructure” of a modern economy, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said investor confidence is essential for sustained economic progress. Company Secretaries, he noted, are at the centre of this architecture and play a vital role in enabling enterprises, start-ups, family businesses and listed companies to grow responsibly.
The Vice-President said strong institutions and sound governance will be as important as physical and digital infrastructure in building a Viksit Bharat. He underlined the complementary role of ICAI, ICMAI and ICSI in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat @2047, describing these professional institutions as key pillars of a strong corporate and economic ecosystem.
Calling for greater opportunities for young people to enter the profession, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated ICSI’s fee-waiver initiatives and urged continued student outreach. He launched the MSME Compliance Calendar 2027 and appreciated ICSI’s initiatives for MSMEs and start-ups, including the ICSI MSME & Start-up Catalyst. He also appreciated ICSI’s contributions to the National Defence Fund under the Shaheed Ki Beti initiative and the Armed Forces Flag Day Fund of the Ministry of Defence, saying, “When the intention is good, everything will be good.”
Concluding, the Vice-President called upon ICSI to continue upholding the trust reposed in the profession and contribute towards building a strong, Aatma-nirbhar and Viksit Bharat @2047. He said India should aspire to become the world’s largest economy, not to dictate terms to others, but “so that no one can dictate unwanted terms to us.” He also invoked the timeless ethos of “Satyam Vada, Dharmam Chara” and extended his greetings to the ICSI fraternity on its Foundation Day.
President, ICSI, C.S. Pawan Chandak; former Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Dr. Sonal Mansingh; and Secretary, ICSI, C.S. Asish Mohan, among others, were present on the occasion.

title: CAQM conducts Inspection Drive along Ring Road in Delhi to assess Road Dust and effectiveness of Road Cleaning Operations
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of its continued efforts to strengthen implementation of dust mitigation measures and improve road cleanliness for effective abatement of air pollution across Delhi-NCR, the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi on 03.10.2026. The inspection was undertaken to assess the presence of visible road dust and the effectiveness of road-cleaning and sweeping operations along the Ring Road.
For the inspection drive, 4 Flying Squad teams constituted by the Commission were deployed to inspect roads under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi. A total of 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer Ring Road were inspected during the drive.
During the inspection, 17 violations of high visible road dust and accumulation of Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste were reported across the inspected road stretches. The observations made during the inspection indicate the need for strict and effective implementation of prescribed road-cleaning, sweeping and dust mitigation measures by the concerned road owning agencies.
The Commission has emphasized that regular and effective road-cleaning and sweeping operations are critical for controlling road dust and preventing its resuspension due to vehicular movement. Accumulation of C&D waste and visible road dust on roadsides and carriageways can contribute to resuspension of dust due to vehicular movement and adversely impact ambient air quality.
PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies are being directed to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. The Commission has further emphasized that road stretches under the jurisdiction of concerned agencies should be maintained in a clean and dust-free condition through regular sweeping, removal of accumulated dust and C&D waste, and timely corrective action.
Inspection drives shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures, identify gaps in compliance and facilitate timely corrective action(s) by the concerned agencies.

title: Union Environment Minister releases two male Great Indian Bustards into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer
subtitle: Milestone outcome of nearly a Decade of Unwavering Dedication of our Scientists, Researchers and Ground Staff: Shri Bhupender Yadav
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 11:33AM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant milestone for the conservation of the critically endangered Great Indian Bustard (GIB), Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today released two male GIBs into the wild at Sam in the Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Rajasthan State Minister for Forest and Environment, Shri Sanjay Sharma, along with senior officers of the Union and State Governments, was present on the occasion.
In a post on X, Shri Yadav thanked Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for his continued guidance, encouragement and support in enabling the scientific community to work towards the conservation of the Great Indian Bustard and other species.
In a milestone move, released two male Great Indian Bustards in Sam, Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, today morning.
This landmark success has been made possible by the nearly decade-long unwavering dedication of our scientists, researchers and ground staff who have spent years…
pic.twitter.com/IiDZzJKyIv
— Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp)
October 4, 2026
The Minister said the milestone is the outcome of nearly a decade of unwavering dedication of our scientists, researchers and ground staff to help the Great Indian Bustard reclaim the deserts of Rajasthan.
The release marks an important transition in India’s GIB conservation programme from establishing a viable conservation-breeding population towards rewilding and augmenting the species in its natural habitat. Learnings from the release would be used to progressively refine the protocols for subsequent releases.
The Bustard Recovery Programme is a collaborative initiative of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Rajasthan Forest Department and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), with technical collaboration from the International Fund for Houbara Conservation and funding support from National CAMPA. The programme focuses on conservation breeding, habitat management, threat mitigation, habitat restoration and community engagement.
The conservation-breeding programme has made significant progress. The GIB facilities at Sam and Ramdevra presently house 97 birds, of which 40 originated from wild-laid eggs and 57 have been bred in captivity. Of these, 86 birds are being maintained for captive reproduction, while 11 have been earmarked for release into the wild. Of these 11, 2 birds were released into the wild at Desert National Park today. Captive reproduction resulted in 24 live chicks in 2025 and 29 in 2026.
Scientific interventions, including the novel ‘jumpstart’ approach, have also contributed to the species’ recovery. Under this approach, captive-laid eggs placed in wild nests were accepted by incubating females, resulting in the hatching of six chicks in Rajasthan and two in Gujarat.
These efforts are being reinforced through habitat restoration by the Rajasthan Forest Department, including the establishment of around 200 sq. km. of fenced grassland enclosures inside the Desert National Park. Long-term telemetry studies by WII have identified these enclosures as prime breeding habitats for the species. The species’ conservation actions are being guided by the Judgement of the Supreme Court of India, based on recommendations of the Expert Committee constituted for this purpose.

title: DRI seizes around 7 kg amphetamine, 5 kg cocaine and 3.5 kg heroin in three operations as it intensifies crackdown on drug trafficking; 5 arrested
subtitle: High-speed chase, cocaine concealed in chocolate tubes and heroin intercepted from passenger in car-pooling taxi mark intelligence-led operations across the country
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Continuing its sustained crackdown on illicit drug trafficking, the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has seized cumulative quantity of 15.59 kg dangerous contraband drugs, Amphetamine, Cocaine and Heroin, in three separate intelligence-led operations conducted on 29–30.09.2026. Five persons have been arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.
In a dramatic operation on 30.09.2026, DRI, along with the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN), intercepted a Mahindra Thar suspected to be carrying Amphetamine at the Ujjain–Dewas Toll Plaza in Madhya Pradesh. On being signalled to stop, the driver broke through the barricade and sped away. The officers pursued the vehicle in a high-speed chase lasting approximately 1.5 hours, before successfully intercepting it near Bicholi Mardana, Indore. Detailed search of the vehicle led to the detection of an ingenious concealment inside the spare (stepney) tyre mounted on the rear door of the Thar. On opening the tyre, officers recovered 21 packets containing 7.116 kg (gross) of whitish-yellow crystalline substance, which tested positive for Amphetamine using the NDPS Field Test Kit. The Amphetamine, along with the vehicle, was seized and all three occupants were arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985.
In another operation on 29.09.2026, DRI intercepted an Indian passenger arriving from Doha at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad, based on specific intelligence regarding smuggling of Cocaine. Examination of his cabin baggage revealed seven chocolate tubes, which appeared unusually heavier than their marked weight. On opening the tubes, officers found 207 light-yellow oval-shaped capsules ingeniously concealed along with the chocolates. Examination of the capsules revealed a white powdery substance which tested positive for Cocaine using the Narcotic Drug Detection Kit. A total
of 4.9 kg (gross) Cocaine
was recovered and seized. The passenger was arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.
In the third operation on 29.09.2026, based on specific intelligence regarding transportation of narcotic drugs DRI officers mounted coordinated surveillance near Phillaur on the outskirts of Jalandhar, Punjab. After checking multiple vehicles near the bridge over the Sutlej river, the suspect was identified travelling as a passenger in a rental car-pooling taxi.
Personal search of the suspect resulted in the recovery of three packets concealed inside a blue backpack kept on his lap, with each packet containing two smaller packets. The substance tested positive for Heroin using a field-testing kit. A total of 3.574 kg heroin was recovered and seized, and the person carrying the contraband was arrested under the NDPS Act, 1985.
The three operations demonstrate DRI's intelligence-led approach in detecting diverse trafficking routes and innovative concealment methods. DRI remains committed to disrupting organised drug-trafficking networks and preventing the movement of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances across the country.

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh to chair the 17th Pension Adalat at IIPA, New Delhi, on 05.10.2026
subtitle:
897 long-pending grievances of super-senior pensioners and family pensioners to be taken up for redressal

Pension Adalat: An Alternative Resolution Mechanism for redressal  of Pension Grievances
ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Pension Adalat is an innovative initiative undertaken by the Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare (DoPPW) for the on-the-spot redressal of grievances of Central Government pensioners. It provides a common platform for all stakeholders concerned with a particular type of grievance to come together for the resolution of long-pending pension grievances. Thus, it works in the spirit of a “Whole-of-Government Approach”. Pension Adalat, an alternate resolution mechanism, helps eliminate the need for expensive and time-consuming court proceedings, thereby offering an efficient and cost-effective grievance redressal mechanism. It is a commitment of the central government to reduce litigation.
Since the introduction by DoPPW in 2017, Pension Adalats have emerged as an efficient and effective mechanism for resolving complicated and long-pending pension grievances. With a success rate of 71.79%, the Pension Adalat initiative has demonstrated its utility by resolving 20,676 out of a total of 28,797 grievances on the spot across its previous 16 editions. The remaining cases have also been redressed subsequent to the respective Pension Adalats through inter-ministerial review meetings conducted by DoPPW.
Continuing this initiative, the Department of Pension and Pensioners’ Welfare will conduct the 17th Pension Adalat under the chairmanship of Hon’ble MoS (PP), Dr. Jitendra Singh, at T. N. Chaturvedi Memorial Hall, IIPA, New Delhi, on 05.10.2026.
This Pension Adalat is unique being thematic in nature, as 897 grievances of super-senior pensioners and family pensioners, pertaining to 24 Ministries/Departments and filed on the CPENGRAMS Portal, have been taken up for redressal.
Super-senior pensioners, family pensioners, and their relatives from across the country will also participate in the proceedings through hybrid mode, as complainants are being provided an opportunity to join the Pension Adalat either physically or through video conferencing.
During the proceedings, Hon’ble MoS (PP) will also release flyers highlighting the success stories of the 16th Pension Adalat, held on 13th May 2026. Further, a booklet containing Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on issues concerning family pensioners will also be released.

title: MoRTH to Organise “Chintan Shivir 2026” to Shape Future-Ready, Safe and High-Quality Highway Infrastructure
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 12:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways will organise Chintan Shivir 2026 on 5–6 October 2026 at Ekta Nagar, Narmada District, Gujarat, bringing together senior representatives from the Centre, States and implementing agencies to deliberate on key issues concerning the development and delivery of highway infrastructure in the country.
The inaugural session on 5 October will feature addresses by Minister of Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari and Ministers of State Shri Ajay Tamta and Shri Harsh Malhotra.
Road Transport and Public Works Ministers from States, along with senior officials of State PWDs, implementing agencies and other stakeholders, have been invited to participate in the Chintan Shivir. Their participation will facilitate Centre-State coordination and exchange of field-level experiences, best practices and practical solutions.
The two-day conclave will focus on identifying key implementation challenges and deliberating on innovative and replicable approaches, along with policy and institutional interventions to improve project delivery, quality, safety and efficiency in the highway sector.
The Chintan Shivir will feature five key thematic sessions covering PM GatiShakti and integrated infrastructure planning; Land Acquisition and Bhoomi Rashi; Model Concession Agreements and Ratings; Designing Safe Highways; and Quality Assurance and Project Monitoring.
The session on PM GatiShakti and integrated infrastructure planning will focus on coordinated and integrated planning for infrastructure development. Discussions on Land Acquisition and Bhoomi Rashi will provide an opportunity to deliberate on issues affecting project implementation and ways to facilitate smoother project execution. The session on Model Concession Agreements and Ratings will focus on relevant contractual and implementation aspects, while Designing Safe Highways will address road safety considerations in highway planning and development. The Quality Assurance and Project Monitoring session will deliberate on measures to strengthen quality, monitoring and project outcomes.
The Chintan Shivir is envisaged as a platform for focused, outcome-oriented deliberations and actionable solutions, strengthening cooperation between the Centre and States and contributing towards the development of safer, higher-quality and future-ready highway infrastructure.

title: Modi government's historic move to provide 3 lakh permanent houses to Andhra Pradesh; Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Shri Chandrababu Naidu sound the clarion call for massive development from Burripalem
subtitle:
The Modi-Naidu duo is a powerful force; Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan declares in Guntur, "Every poor person in Andhra Pradesh will have a permanent home."

A new beginning for the nation's housing revolution from Guntur: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu inaugurate the country's first 3D-printed housing project.

"If I am 'Mama' (maternal uncle) to MP, I am 'Mama' to AP as well": Shivraj Singh Chouhan wins hearts amidst a crowd of thousands in Guntur, stating that serving the people is akin to worshipping God.

Andhra Pradesh set to become India's number one state under Modi's vision and Naidu's leadership; scripting a new chapter of development from Amaravati to Polavaram – Shri Shivraj Singh.

From 'Annadata Sukhi Bhava' (May the farmer prosper) to 'Lakhpati Didi' (women earning over a lakh annually)—the Modi-Naidu government is economically empowering farmers and women – Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan.

"The Telugu language is sweeter than honey": Shivraj Singh Chouhan's heartwarming Telugu address in Burripalem draws thunderous applause from the public.

National 'SARAS Mela' to be held in Andhra Pradesh—the first time outside Delhi—on October 15th; Honorable president will inaugurate a grand event celebrating the 'Nakshatra Didis' (empowered women entrepreneurs) – Shri Shivraj Singh.

Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu welcomes the Union Minister... "Instead of 75,000, 'Mama Maharaj' sanctioned 3 lakh houses—a major gift for Andhra"
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Giving fresh momentum to the holistic and rural development of Andhra Pradesh, Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, presided over a significant event in Burripalem village, Guntur district, on Sunday. A major initiative involving the construction of 3 lakh permanent houses at a cost of ₹3,600 crore in the state was launched. In the distinguished presence of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu, the Union Minister laid the foundation stone for a pilot project comprising 177 houses built using the country's first 3D construction technology. Addressing a massive gathering, Shri Chouhan remarked that the 'dynamic partnership' between Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in Delhi and Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu in Amaravati is driving '360-degree development' to make the state the number one in the country.
A new milestone in rural development was achieved on Sunday in the historic village of Burripalem (Tenali Mandal) in Andhra Pradesh's Guntur district. Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Shri Nara Chandrababu Naidu jointly launched housing projects for 3 lakh permanent houses under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Gramin 2.0). Additionally, a pilot project featuring the country's first 3D-constructed houses—built at a cost of ₹14 crore—was inaugurated.  The event was attended by Union Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications Dr. Pemmasani; Andhra Pradesh Ministers Mr. Nadendla Manohar (Civil Supplies), Mr. Kolusu Parthasarathy (Housing and Information), and Mr. Kandula Durgesh (Tourism); BJP State President Mr. PN Madhav; Mr. Lingamneni Ramesh; MLC Mr. Lapati Prasad; and School Secretary Mr. Bathu Tatya Babu; alongside senior officials from the Central and Andhra Pradesh governments and thousands of villagers, farmers, and women.
3 Lakh Houses Provided Instead of 76,000; "If 9 Lakh Are Requested, We Will Provide Those Too," Says Minister
Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced, "Officials from my ministry had informed me of a quota of only 76,000 houses for Andhra Pradesh. However, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu stated that he wanted to fulfill the dream of every poor person in his state and required more houses. With Prime Minister Modi's blessings, we have handed over the first installment for 3 lakh permanent houses—not just 76,000—directly to Andhra." He added, "Babu smiled and said, 'The heart wants more'; we need another 6 lakh houses. I told him, 'Babu, the entire Government of India is yours, and I am yours too. Complete these 3 lakh houses, and immediately afterward, another 3 lakh and then another 3 lakh houses will be sanctioned. Every single poor person in Andhra will get a permanent house.'"
3D Concrete Technology: Sturdy Houses to be Ready in 6 Months
Describing the 3D concrete printing project launching in Burripalem and Obulanaidupalem as a housing revolution for the country, he noted that this pilot project would result in significant savings in time, cost, and labor. Using machinery and advanced technology, these houses will be completed in just six months, boasting durability and longevity far superior to traditional homes.
PM Modi Grants Legal Status to Amaravati
Shri Chouhan stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi secured the status of Andhra Pradesh's sole permanent capital for Amaravati by passing legislation in Parliament and released special financial assistance of ₹15,000 crore. The lifeline project of Polavaram is now being completed at full speed with a 100% grant from the Central Government. Additionally, the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport will take the state's connectivity to new heights.
'Annadata Sukhi Bhava' and the Mission for 60 Lakh 'Lakhpati Didis'
Highlighting the empowerment of farmers and women, Union Minister Shri Chouhan noted that Chief Minister Naidu has supplemented the Central Government's ₹6,000 PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi with ₹14,000 under the 'Annadata Sukhi Bhava' scheme, thereby providing farmers with historic annual financial assistance of ₹20,000. He stated that Andhra would be developed into the country's largest horticulture hub for fruits, flowers, vegetables, and medicinal crops. Discussing self-help groups, he mentioned that 23 lakh women in the state have already become 'Lakhpati Didis' (women earning an annual income of over ₹1 lakh), a figure the NDA government aims to raise to 60 lakh. He announced that for the first time in the country's history, the national 'SARAS Mela' is being organized outside Delhi—in Andhra Pradesh—on October 15, and it will be inaugurated by President Smt. Droupadi Murmu herself.
'If I am MP's Mama, then I am AP's Mama too': Greeting in Telugu
Upon taking the stage, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan began his address in fluent Telugu, accompanied by chants of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Shri Venkateswara Bhagwan Ki Jai." He described the land of Andhra as a confluence of knowledge, science, talent, and rich traditions. Paying obeisance to this sacred land—the home of Tenali Ram—he said, "The Telugu language is sweeter than honey, and today it is carving a unique identity for itself across India. If I am the 'Mama' (maternal uncle) of Madhya Pradesh, then I am the 'Mama' of Andhra Pradesh as well. For me, serving the people is akin to worshipping God. Witnessing the spirit, honesty, and passion of the people here, only one thought arises from the heart: 'Truly, one longs to meet you all!'"
Appreciation for Dr. Pemmasani’s Simplicity and Chief Minister Naidu’s Vision
Union Minister Shivraj Singh expressed great delight upon visiting Burripalem, the ancestral village of his colleague, Union Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani. He remarked with a touch of humor, "Initially, I wondered—since Chandra Sekhar ji is 'America-returned'—whether he would grasp village life and rural development. However, I was amazed by his deep connection with the people, his spirit of service, and the clarity of his work. 'Babu' (Chandrababu Naidu) truly identifies talent, nurtures it, and brings it into the political arena for public service." He described Chandrababu Naidu as the embodiment of dynamic, dedicated, and decisive leadership. It was Naidu who transformed Andhra into a global IT hub, and today, that same visionary approach is establishing Amaravati as a premier destination for AI, quantum technology, data centers, and advanced manufacturing.
Address by Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu
Expressing his gratitude to Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Chief Minister Shri Chandrababu Naidu stated that Shivraj ji is not only the beloved 'Mama' (maternal uncle) of Madhya Pradesh but also of the entire state of Andhra Pradesh. He said, "Shivraj ji is a mass leader who has set an unbeatable record in Madhya Pradesh through his good governance and dedication to service. Today, as soon as we raised the issue of providing permanent housing for the state's poor, he won the hearts of the people of Andhra by instantly approving 3 lakh houses—far exceeding the initial proposal of 75,000. When I mentioned the NDA's pledge to ensure a permanent roof over every head and noted our requirement for a total of 9 lakh houses, he promised in the public gathering that the Central Government would immediately sanction the remaining 6 lakh houses as soon as the first phase of work is completed.”
Chief Minister Mr. Naidu expressed confidence that, under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and with the continuous support of Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Andhra Pradesh will emerge as the country's number-one state across all fronts—including infrastructure, agriculture, modern technology, and rural development.

title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan Hands Over 3 Lakh Houses Worth ₹3,600 Crore to Andhra Pradesh, Lays Foundation for India’s First 3D Concrete-Printed Housing Project
subtitle:
Modi Government Sanctions 3 Lakh Houses Worth ₹3,600 Crore for Andhra Pradesh; Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Chandrababu Naidu Lead Development Push

“Modi-Naidu Partnership Is a Force Multiplier”: Shivraj Singh Chouhan Assures Permanent Homes for Every Poor Family in Andhra Pradesh

India’s First 3D Concrete-Printed Housing Project Launched in Andhra Pradesh; Chouhan, Naidu Lay Foundation in Guntur

“If I Am MP’s Mama, I Am AP’s Mama Too”: Shivraj Singh Chouhan Wins Hearts with Telugu Address in Guntur

Andhra Pradesh Set to Become India’s No. 1 State Under Modi’s Vision and Naidu’s Leadership: Shivraj Singh Chouhan

From ‘Annadata Sukhibhava’ to ‘Lakhpati Didi’: Modi-Naidu Governments Empower Farmers and Women, Says Shivraj Singh Chouhan
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Guntur (Andhra Pradesh)/New Delhi | October 4, 2026 | Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Sunday handed over the first instalment of 3 lakh houses worth ₹3,600 crore to Andhra Pradesh under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Gramin 2.0 at an event in Burripalem village of Guntur district. In the presence of Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, Chouhan also laid the foundation stone for the country’s first pilot housing project using 3D concrete printing technology, comprising 177 houses at a cost of ₹14 crore. Addressing thousands of people at the gathering, Chouhan said the Centre and the Andhra Pradesh government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu, are working together to accelerate the state’s development across all sectors and make it the number one state in the country. The event was attended by Union Minister of State for Rural Development and Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Andhra Pradesh Minister for Civil Supplies Nadendla Manohar, Minister for Housing and Information Kolusu Parthasarathy, Minister for Tourism Kandula Durgesh, BJP state president P.V.N. Madhav, Rajya Sabha MP Bhashyam Ramakrishna, MP Lingamneni Ramesh, MLC Alapati Rajendra Prasad, Housing Corporation Chairman Bathula Tataiah Babu, senior officials from the Central and state governments, and thousands of farmers, rural residents and women.
Centre increases housing allocation from 76,000 to 3 lakh houses
Highlighting the Centre’s commitment to meeting the housing needs of Andhra Pradesh, Shri Chouhan said the initial allocation proposed by officials was only 76,000 houses. However, following Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu’s request to ensure that every poor family in the state had a permanent home, the allocation was increased to 3 lakh houses. “Our ministry officials had informed me that Andhra Pradesh was eligible for only 76,000 houses. But Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu insisted that every poor family in the state should have a permanent home and requested more houses. With the blessings of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, we have sanctioned 3 lakh houses instead of 76,000,” he said. Chouhan added that Naidu had also sought another 6 lakh houses. Assuring the Chief Minister of the Centre’s continued support, he said, “I told Babu that the entire Government of India is with you, and I am also with you. Complete the construction of these 3 lakh houses, and we will sanction another 3 lakh, followed by a further 3 lakh. Every poor family in Andhra Pradesh will have a permanent house.”
3D concrete printing to deliver durable houses in six months
Describing the 3D concrete printing housing project at Burripalem and Obulnayudupalem as a major step towards modernising rural housing, Chouhan said the ₹14-crore pilot project would significantly reduce construction time, costs and labour requirements. The project will use advanced machinery and 3D concrete printing technology to construct 177 houses, with construction expected to be completed within six months. The houses are designed to offer greater durability and a longer lifespan compared to conventional construction methods.
Centre supports Amaravati, Polavaram and infrastructure development
Referring to the state’s political and developmental history, Chouhan said Andhra Pradesh had been left without a capital following the division of the state in 2014. He said the Modi government had passed legislation in Parliament recognising Amaravati as the sole permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh and had extended special financial assistance of ₹15,000 crore for its development. Chouhan also highlighted the Polavaram irrigation project, describing it as a lifeline for the state. He said the project, which had faced delays under the previous government, was now progressing with 100% grant assistance from the Centre. He added that the proposed Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport would further strengthen connectivity and support the state’s economic growth.
‘Annadata Sukhibhava’ strengthens farmers’ income; 60 lakh Lakhpati Didis targeted
Highlighting the state’s efforts to improve farmers’ incomes, Chouhan said the Centre’s annual assistance of ₹6,000 under the PM-KISAN scheme, combined with the Andhra Pradesh government’s ₹14,000 assistance under the ‘Annadata Sukhibhava’ scheme, would provide farmers with ₹20,000 annually. He said Andhra Pradesh had the potential to emerge as the country’s leading horticulture hub, with a focus on fruits, flowers, vegetables and medicinal crops. On women’s economic empowerment, Chouhan said 23 lakh women in Andhra Pradesh had already become Lakhpati Didis through self-help groups. The NDA government aims to increase this number to 60 lakh, expanding livelihood opportunities and strengthening women’s financial independence. He also announced that the national Saras Mela would be organised in Andhra Pradesh on October 15, marking the first time the event would be held outside Delhi. President Droupadi Murmu will inaugurate the event, which will provide a platform for women-led self-help groups to showcase their products and expand market access.
‘If I am MP’s Mama, I am also AP’s Mama’: Chouhan greets people in Telugu
Beginning his address with chants of ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’ and ‘Sri Venkateswara Bhagwan Ki Jai’, Chouhan greeted the gathering in Telugu and praised Andhra Pradesh for its rich heritage, knowledge, scientific achievements and talent. Paying tribute to the land of Tenali Ramakrishna, he said the Telugu language was sweeter than honey and was gaining recognition across the country. “If I am the Mama of Madhya Pradesh, I am also the Mama of Andhra Pradesh. Serving the people is a form of worship for me. Seeing the enthusiasm, honesty and passion of the people here, I can only say that I truly wish to meet you again,” he said, drawing an enthusiastic response from the gathering.
Chouhan praises Pemmasani’s grassroots connect and Naidu’s leadership
Chouhan expressed particular happiness at visiting Burripalem, the ancestral village of Union Minister of State Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani. Praising Pemmasani’s commitment to public service and his connection with people at the grassroots, he said he had initially wondered whether someone who had returned from the United States would understand rural life and development. “However, seeing his close connect with the people, his spirit of service and his clarity of purpose, I was truly impressed. Babu has a remarkable ability to identify talent and bring capable people into public service,” he said. Describing Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu as a dynamic, dedicated and decisive leader, Chouhan credited him with establishing Andhra Pradesh as a major IT hub. He said Naidu’s vision was now driving the development of Amaravati as a centre for artificial intelligence, quantum technology, data centres and advanced manufacturing.
Chandrababu Naidu thanks Centre for housing support
Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu thanked Chouhan for his support and described him as a beloved ‘Mama’ not only for the people of Madhya Pradesh but also for the people of Andhra Pradesh. “Shivraj Singh Chouhan is a people’s leader who has set an exceptional record through good governance and public service in Madhya Pradesh. When we raised the issue of providing permanent homes to the poor in Andhra Pradesh, he immediately increased the allocation from around 75,000 houses to 3 lakh, winning the hearts of the people of the state,” Naidu said. He added that the NDA government was committed to ensuring a permanent roof over every poor family and that the state required a total of 9 lakh houses. Referring to Chouhan’s assurance, Naidu said the remaining 6 lakh houses would also be sanctioned by the Centre as soon as the first phase was completed. Expressing confidence in the state’s development trajectory, Naidu said that under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and with the continued support of Chouhan, Andhra Pradesh would emerge as the country’s number one state in infrastructure, agriculture, advanced technology and rural development.

title: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Hosts Lunch for Delhi based Medical Alumni from Jammu, Recalls His Days as Professor in GMC Jammu
subtitle:
Former Students, Now Senior Doctors and Medical Professionals, Reunite with Their Teacher in Delhi

GMC Jammu Alumni Serving in Senior Positions Across Leading Hospitals and Healthcare Institutions

Dr. Jitendra Singh Recalls His Association with Medicine and Diabetes Before Entering Public Life Full-Time

Former Students Share Professional Journeys and Recall Their Classroom Days with Their Teacher
date:

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences and MoS PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today hosted a luncheon interaction at his New Delhi residence for a group of Delhi based medical alumni from Jammu, most of them from Government Medical College, Jammu, many of whom had been his students during his years as Professor of Medicine and Diabetes.
The gathering brought together former students who have gone on to build successful medical careers and are now serving in senior positions across hospitals and healthcare institutions in Delhi-NCR and other parts of the region.
Recalling his association with Government Medical College, Jammu, before taking up full time to public life, Dr. Jitendra Singh said it was particularly gratifying to meet his former students and see how well they had progressed in their professional lives. The doctors shared their experiences and recalled their days as students, making the lunch a warm reunion with their former teacher.
The gathering brought together medical professionals from diverse specialities, including medicine, neurology, pulmonary medicine, oncology, psychiatry, pharmacology, paediatrics, gastroenterology, hepatology, radiology, ophthalmology, plastic surgery and hospital administration. Many of the former students are today serving in senior clinical, academic and administrative positions across leading hospitals and medical institutions.
Among those present were Dr. Sheikh Yasir Islam, Professor of Medicine, Lady Hardinge Medical College; Dr. Sumbul Erum, Private Practice, Noida; Dr. Sujata Thapa, Professor of Medicine, RML Hospital; Dr. Padma Lahdol, Assistant Professor of Medicine, RML Hospital; Dr. Akhil, Associate Professor of Neurology, Lady Hardinge Medical College; Dr. Atul, Oncologist, Max Hospital, Noida; Dr. Ekta Arora, Associate Professor, GIMS; Dr. Sanjay Fotedar, Professor of Pulmonary Medicine, Rohtak; Dr. Shikhaa Mahajan, Professor, SHKM Government Medical College, Mewat; Dr. Heena Kudyar, Plastic Surgeon, Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj; and Dr. Himani Kudyar, Pathologist associated with multiple diagnostic centres in Gurugram.

P. Byotra, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; and Dr. Namita Kaul, Senior Neurologist, Medanta Hospital, Noida.
The former students recalled attending Dr. Jitendra Singh’s classes and shared memories of their academic years at Government Medical College, Jammu. The lunch provided an opportunity for them to reconnect after several years, share their professional journeys and express their gratitude to their teacher for the academic foundation and guidance received during their formative years.
From specialised clinical care to medical education and healthcare administration, the former students have pursued diverse professional paths and continue to contribute to the healthcare sector in different capacities. Their journeys span several areas of medicine and include service at prominent hospitals and academic institutions across Delhi-NCR and neighbouring regions.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said that for a teacher, seeing a student's progress in life, attain senior positions and make a meaningful contribution to society is among the most fulfilling aspects of the profession. He expressed happiness at the achievements of his former students and their continued contribution to healthcare.
The lunch gathering brought together a teacher and his former students in a warm reunion that celebrated their shared academic past and the professional journeys they have undertaken since their days at Government Medical College, Jammu.

title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal to Flag Off First International Cargo Voyage from Dibrugarh
subtitle: Maiden methanol voyage from Bogibeel to Dhaka via National Waterway-2 marks a new chapter for Assam's river trade since Independence
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 9:22PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal
, will flag off the first international cargo voyage from Dibrugarh tomorrow, 5 October 2026, at 11:00 AM at Bogibeel Terminal, Dibrugarh. The
Chief Minister of Assam, Dr. Himanta Biswa Sarma
, will join the ceremony virtually as Chief Guest.
The maiden voyage will carry methanol produced by Assam Petro-Chemicals Limited (APCL) from Bogibeel to Pangaon Port in Dhaka, Bangladesh, via National Waterway-2 (river Brahmaputra) and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route (IBPR). It will be the first time since Independence that a cargo consignment sails from Dibrugarh to a foreign port.
For generations before Independence, the Brahmaputra was Upper Assam's main link to the markets of the world, and Dibrugarh was among the region's most important river ports. Tomorrow's flag-off marks the return of that link, reflecting the Government's push to develop inland waterways as a cheaper, greener and more efficient mode of transport for the Northeast.
The ceremony will be attended by
Charan Boro, Minister of Transport, Government of Assam; Rameswar Teli, Minister of Labour Welfare, Government of Assam
; and
Bimal Borah, Minister of Industries, Commerce and Public Enterprises, Government of Assam
, as Special Guests.
Presence of Terash Gowalla, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha); MLAs Prasanta Phukan (Dibrugarh), Chakradhar Gogoi (Khowang), Sanjoy Kishan (Makum), Suren Phukan (Digboi), Binod Hazarika (Chabua-Lahowal), Bhaskar Sharma (Margherita), Taranga Gogoi (Naharkatia) and Pulok Gohain (Tinsukia); Sushil Kumar Lohani, Chairman, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI); and Bikul Ch. Deka, Chairman, APCL is also expected.
The event is being organised by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and IWAI, together with the Government of Assam and APCL.
The ceremony will be streamed live on IWAI’s official YouTube channel, IWAI_ShipMin. More information on iwai.gov.in and through IWAI’s official social media handles on X, LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook.

title: Reforms aimed at empowering cotton farmers, enhancing transparency and strengthening India’s cotton value chain to take centre stage
subtitle:
Digital procurement, quality improvement, traceability, HDPS and Kasturi Cotton initiatives to be showcased

Farmers, industry stakeholders and policymakers to share experiences and outcomes of reforms
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ministry of Textile, Government of India through its Cotton Corporation of India Ltd. (CCI), a Public Sector Undertaking, will organize a special showcase event on
6th October 2026
in
Hyderabad, Telangana
, as part of
‘Reform Utsav 2026’. The event will showcase the transformative reforms undertaken by CCI, in coordination with the Ministry of Textiles, to make the cotton procurement ecosystem more farmer-centric, transparent, technology-driven and efficient
.
The event will bring together senior government officials, representatives of the Government of Telangana, policymakers, farmers, industry associations and other stakeholders from the cotton and textile sectors. It will provide a platform to highlight the impact of reforms on the ground and facilitate experience-sharing among key stakeholders across the cotton value chain.
Over the past few years, CCI has undertaken a series of technology-enabled and institutional reforms covering cotton procurement, farmer registration, digital slot booking, direct payments, quality assessment, traceability, sale of cotton and stakeholder engagement. These interventions are aimed at improving ease of doing business, strengthening transparency and accountability, and ensuring more efficient delivery of services to cotton farmers.
A key highlight of the event will be a presentation on CCI’s major reforms and initiatives
,
followed by the screening of a short film capturing their implementation and impact. The showcase will demonstrate how digital technologies and process re-engineering are transforming traditional systems and creating a more seamless interface between farmers, CCI, ginners and the textile industry
.
The event will also feature experience-sharing by cotton farmers and industry stakeholders, providing an opportunity to hear directly from those participating in and benefiting from the reforms. The discussions will cover important initiatives relating to cotton quality improvement, High-Density Planting System (HDPS), Kasturi Cotton Bharat, digitalization of cotton procurement and other measures for strengthening the cotton value chain
.
The Kapas Kisan digital platform will be among the key initiatives showcased. The platform has brought together various stages of cotton procurement through digital processes, including farmer registration, slot booking, procurement-related communication and Aadhaar-enabled payments. Such initiatives are aimed at enhancing transparency, reducing procedural complexities and providing farmers with greater visibility over the procurement process.
The event will also highlight CCI’s efforts towards quality improvement and traceability of Indian cotton, including initiatives for contamination control, digital traceability and promotion of premium-quality cotton under the Kasturi Cotton Bharat initiative. These measures seek to enhance the identity, quality and market positioning of Indian cotton and strengthen its acceptance in domestic and international markets.
The showcase will further draw attention to the High-Density Planting System (HDPS) and other productivity-oriented interventions being promoted in collaboration with relevant agricultural institutions. These initiatives seek to address the productivity gap in Indian cotton and contribute towards improving farm-level returns and the overall competitiveness of the Indian cotton sector.
The Central Silk Board (CSB), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is driving transformative reforms through digital service delivery, mission-mode technology transfer and innovative outreach, making Indian sericulture more accessible, efficient and stakeholder-centric.
1. Digitisation of Silk Mark Services
– Ease of Doing Business: The Silk Mark Organization of India (SMOI), implementing the Silk Mark Scheme since 2004, assures the authenticity of pure silk through the Silk Mark. From 2022–23, SMOI progressively digitised registration, renewal, document processing, pre-inspection, payments, label indenting and issuance, record management and grievance redressal.
The system now serves 7,000+ Authorised Users, with 500+ new enrolments annually. Applications can generally be processed within 1–2 working days, subject to fulfilment of prescribed requirements. The reform has reduced paperwork and physical visits while enhancing transparency, traceability and administrative efficiency, particularly benefiting MSMEs and silk-sector stakeholders.
2. Mera Resham Mera Abhimaan
– A Mega Sericulture Technology Transfer Campaign: The Central Silk Board (CSB) launched Mera Resham Mera Abhimaan (MRMA) during 2025 as a 100-day Mega Sericulture Technology Transfer Campaign, taking proven technologies from “Lab to Land” through direct farmer engagement, demonstrations, training and field-level interventions across 129 districts in 26 States/UTs. MRMA 1.0 reached 75,000 farmers through 1,400+ programmes.
Building on the achievements and learnings of MRMA 1.0, MRMA 2.0 was designed as a evolved, structured and impact-oriented campaign, covering 218 key sericulture districts contributing over 95% of India’s raw silk production. It integrates baseline surveys, stakeholder consultations, District Sericulture Development Plans, target-oriented and need-based action plans and a dynamic interactive MRMA web portal. More than 1,700 programmes have been conducted, directly reaching 73,000+ farmers and approximately one lakh stakeholders through digital platforms.
3. Seri-Tourism
– An Experience from Farm to Fibre: CSB has conceptualised Seri-Tourism to integrate sericulture, tourism, education and local economic development, showcasing the complete “Soil-to-Silk” journey through museums, live demonstrations, host-plant and moth parks, technology displays and product outlets.
The CSB-P4 Basic Seed Farm, Manasbal, Jammu & Kashmir, and CSB-Eri Basic Seed Farm, Topatoli, Assam, are being developed as Seri-Tourism Hubs, showcasing silk diversity, germplasm conservation, silkworm rearing, cocoon production, reeling, weaving, dyeing and Silk Mark awareness.
A New Paradigm
Together, these reforms are creating a modern, technology-enabled and stakeholder-centric sericulture ecosystem—where services are digital, technologies reach the last mile, and India’s silk heritage becomes an experiential asset, generating new opportunities for farmers, MSMEs, artisans, entrepreneurs and local communities.
The reforms being showcased at
Reform Utsav 2026
reflect the Government’s broader vision of building a stronger and more integrated textile value chain — from Farm to Fibre, Fibre to Factory, Factory to Fashion and Fashion to Foreign.
The Hyderabad event will provide an important platform for taking the reform journey from policy and institutional interventions to field-level outcomes, while encouraging greater participation and collaboration among farmers, industry, government agencies and knowledge institutions.
Through these reforms, CCI continues to strengthen its role as a key institutional pillar of India’s cotton economy, supporting farmers, improving procurement systems, facilitating quality enhancement and contributing to a more transparent, efficient, sustainable and globally competitive cotton and textile ecosystem.
Reform Utsav 2026
is part of the Ministry of Textiles’ initiative to showcase transformative reforms undertaken by its organizations and institutions, and to highlight their impact on citizens, farmers, industry and the wider textile ecosystem.

title: MY Bharat Organises “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” Nationwide
subtitle: Over 1 Lakh Youth and Citizens Participate Across More Than 150 Locations
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:

                04 OCT 2026 11:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of the “Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat” Abhiyan, MY Bharat and its partner organisations organised “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” on October 4, 2026, across more than 150 locations nationwide, witnessing the enthusiastic participation of over 1 lakh youth and citizens.
The nationwide initiative aimed to create widespread awareness among youth and communities about the harmful effects of substance abuse and to promote healthy, responsible and addiction-free lifestyles. The programme brought together young people, citizens, public representatives and partner organisations to reinforce the message of collective responsibility in building a healthier and drug-free society.
As part of the initiative, participants took part in 3–5 km walks, Nukkad Nataks, slogan writing, heritage walks and other youth-led awareness activities. These activities used public spaces and community participation to spread awareness about the risks associated with substance abuse and encourage young people to make healthy and responsible lifestyle choices.
Several programmes also featured the Nasha Mukt Yuva Pledge, through which participants committed themselves to staying away from substance abuse and contributing towards creating a healthy, aware and drug-free society. The pledge further strengthened the campaign's emphasis on individual responsibility and collective action against substance abuse.
The nationwide programme also witnessed the participation of several public representatives and dignitaries, adding further momentum and visibility to the campaign. The key dignitaries who participated included 2 Lieutenant Governors, 1 Cabinet Minister, 8 Members of Parliament and 8 Members of Legislative Assemblies.
The enthusiastic participation of youth, citizens, public representatives and partner organisations across the country reflects the growing collective resolve to build a Nasha Mukt Yuva for a Viksit Bharat. The initiative reinforces the vision of empowering young people to lead healthier lives and become active contributors to a healthier, stronger and developed India.
The “Walk for Nasha Mukt Yuva” is part of the broader Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Abhiyan, which seeks to mobilise youth and communities through sustained awareness, participation and collective action against substance abuse.

title: India’s Rising Supercomputing Ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                04 OCT 2026 5:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s supercomputing journey has evolved from PARAM 8000 in the early 1990s to a national ecosystem under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM), launched in 2015. With 40 supercomputers delivering 68
PF as of September 2026, NSM is expanding access to high-performance computing (HPC). The Mission has also developed indigenous servers, software, cooling and networking technologies, while supporting applications in Computational Biology, Weather Prediction and Climate Modelling, Disaster Management, Big Data Analytics, and Astrophysics.
Building India’s Supercomputing Capabilities
From predicting crop yields and tracking disease outbreaks to accelerating drug discovery and predicting affected areas due to river floods, high-performance computing supports societal applications that affect everyday life. They help process massive datasets and support complex simulations across climate, space, healthcare and engineering. They also enable faster analysis and help researchers address increasingly complex scientific challenges. It is becoming essential for accelerating scientific discovery and technological innovation.
Supercomputers are high-performance computing systems designed to process complex calculations at exceptional speeds. They combine large numbers of processors to perform multiple calculations simultaneously. This enables researchers to analyse massive datasets and run sophisticated simulations efficiently. Supercomputers therefore provide critical infrastructure for advanced scientific research and strategic applications.
India’s growing digital ecosystem is driving demand for advanced computing infrastructure. India generates nearly
20% of the world’s data
. Applications such as Artificial Intelligence, weather forecasting and space research require significant computing capabilities. The Government is therefore expanding access to supercomputing across research institutions. This effort strengthens indigenous capabilities and supports India’s vision of
Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies
ESTIC-2026, the second edition of India’s Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave, will be held from 27–29 October 2026. The event will be held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme
“Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies.”
Organised by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR), ESTIC-2026 will advance emerging science and technology frontiers. These include
Supercomputing
and other emerging technologies. The conclave will catalyse strategic collaborations and support India’s vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. Spanning 12 thematic areas, the event will feature plenary sessions, technical discussions and exhibitions.
Read More on Agenda:
ESTIC 2026
The Strategy Behind National Supercomputing Mission
India launched the
National Supercomputing Mission (NSM)
in April 2015 to strengthen the country’s computing capabilities. The Mission was launched with an outlay of about
₹
4,500 crore
.
It is jointly steered by the
Department of Science and Technology (DST)
and the
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
.
The Mission aims to build self-reliance in supercomputing and strengthen India’s high-performance computing capabilities. It promotes the use of supercomputing for research, development and problem-solving across scientific and technological domains. It also supports the development of solutions for societal applications. The Mission seeks to establish a globally competitive supercomputing ecosystem in India.
The
Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Pune
,
and the
Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru
,
implement the Mission. NSM follows a 'Build approach' consisting of three concurrent phases to create indigenous supercomputing infrastructure
:
assembly, manufacturing, and design and manufacturing support
.
This approach combines the expansion of computing infrastructure with the development of indigenous capabilities.
Interesting Facts About the Supercomputers
Unlike regular computers, supercomputers are designed to process large amounts of data at very high speeds. They use multiple processors or computing nodes that work together simultaneously. This allows them to solve complex problems much faster than conventional computers. High-speed connections between these nodes enable them to exchange data efficiently during large-scale computations.
Supercomputers are sometimes called
parallel computers
because supercomputing can use parallel processing. Parallel processing is when multiple CPUs work on solving a single calculation at a given time.
A supercomputer's power is measured in
FLOPS (Floating Point Operations Per Second)
. This tells us how many calculations it can perform in one second. One teraFLOPS (TF) means one trillion calculations per second, while one petaFLOPS (PF) means one quadrillion calculations per second.
The
world’s fastest supercomputer
achieves around 2.19 exaflops in 2026. It can perform about 2.19 quintillion calculations per second.
Current Status of the Mission
Under NSM, India has established an ecosystem focused on achieving self-reliance in supercomputing. It covers supercomputer design, development, manufacturing, system software and specialised applications. This growing indigenous capability can reduce dependence on imported technologies. It also strengthens India’s domestic high-performance computing ecosystem.
NSM plans to establish a total of 50
supercomputers with a cumulative capacity exceeding 123 PF across various academic/research institutions across India.
These systems cater to diverse computational requirements based on their processing capacities.
Evolution of PARAM Series
PARAM 8000, developed by C-DAC and unveiled in 1991, marked India’s entry into indigenous supercomputing with a speed of 1 gigaflop. It laid the foundation for the PARAM series, which evolved through increasingly powerful systems such as PARAM Yuva at 54 teraflops, supporting computationally intensive applications. This supported applications such as weather forecasting, which predicts atmospheric conditions, and computational fluid dynamics, which studies fluid flow, etc. The series later expanded India’s supercomputing capabilities for both domestic research and international deployments.
Expanding Computing Capacity
As of September 2026, India had deployed 40
supercomputers with a combined capacity of 68 PF.
This includes 13
high-end systems exceeding 1 PF
.
Additionally,
12
mid-range systems have capacities between 500 TF and 1 PF
.
Another 15
systems have capacities below 500 TF
.
These machines have been built locally and commissioned across the country. The Mission continues to advance infrastructure, applications, research and development, and human resource development.
Supercomputing for Sustainable Development
NSM contributes to 11 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by applying advanced computing to areas of national development. Its applications support climate action through flood prediction, forest-fire management and climate modelling, while strengthening education and skill development through HPC training. The Mission also promotes innovation, indigenous technology, economic growth and collaboration among academia, industry and research institutions.
National Applications of Supercomputing under NSM
Supercomputers deployed under NSM support large-scale simulations and fast data processing, enabling national applications across various sectors.
Genomics and Drug Discovery Platform
: It studies large sets of molecules to help find and test drugs. It was used during COVID-19 to screen existing drugs and also predict side effects like heart risk.
Urban Environment Decision Support System:
It uses detailed models to track weather and air pollution. It predicts heavy rain and pollution so cities can prepare and mitigate damage.
Seismic Imaging Suite:
It aims to improve oil and gas exploration by using advanced algorithms to map subsurface structures. Its performance matches commercial seismic imaging tools.
Early Warning System for Flood Prediction for River Basins:
It leverages data analysis and predictive models to forecast floods up to 2 days in advance. It is being used for the Mahanadi River basin to protect communities and infrastructure.
The Forest Fire Spread Model
: It combines satellite remote sensing with computational models to predict how forest fires will spread. It has been tested in regions like the Sikkim Himalayas using a HPC system.
Materials Science and Computational Chemistry Applications
: It provides a suite that allows simulations of atoms, molecules, and alloys. These facilitate the study of their behaviour.
These applications demonstrate how India’s growing HPC infrastructure is strengthening research, supporting evidence-based decision-making and addressing complex challenges across health, environment, energy and advanced science.
Achievements: Indigenous Components Developed Under NSM
Under the NSM, a complete ecosystem has been established with the focused goal of achieving self-reliance in supercomputing. It includes, inter alia, the design, development, and manufacturing of critical supercomputing sub-components, as follows:
Rudra Series of Servers:
It is a key supercomputing component. It provides the processing power needed to run complex calculations, simulations and AI workloads. It has been indigenously designed and developed by C-DAC, with its technology transferred to Indian Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) partners for manufacturing.
PARAM Rudra Series: Advancing Indigenous Supercomputing
A major milestone of NSM has been the development of the PARAM Rudra supercomputers, built using indigenously designed and manufactured Rudra servers and an indigenous system software stack. They support a wide range of applications like advanced research in astronomy, material science, atomic physics, and earth sciences. As of September 2026, 6,000 Rudra servers had been deployed in PARAM Rudra supercomputers, with another 1,500 servers under manufacturing.
High-Speed Interconnect Network
:
A high-speed inter-communication network between computer nodes has been developed and tested with speeds of 100 Gbps and 200 Gbps. It enhances data transfer and communication between computing nodes, strengthening India’s supercomputing capabilities.
Indigenous Cooling Technology:
Cooling technology has been indigenously developed and demonstrated and is now in the deployment stage. It is important for maintaining the operating temperature of high-performance computing systems and have better power efficiency.
High Performance Computing (HPC) System Software:
A complete HPC system software stack has been developed and integrated with supercomputing systems to support their efficient operation and management.
PARAM Shavak:
It is a
supercomputing-in-a-box
that has been designed, developed and manufactured in India to meet the HPC and AI computing needs of students and researchers in engineering colleges and universities.
HPC Applications for National Needs:
HPC applications have been developed and deployed across areas such as genomics and drug discovery. These applications support organisations including the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Central Water Commission (CWC), Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), and the Ministry of AYUSH.
From core computing infrastructure to applications addressing national needs, NSM is expanding India’s capacity to develop and use advanced computing technologies within the country.
Building a Skilled Workforce for High-Performance Computing in India
As access to supercomputing infrastructure expands, NSM is also building the skills needed to use these resources effectively. NSM infrastructure has supported over 16,000 researchers, including more than 2,900 PhD scholars, across over 400 institutions. These systems have executed more than 1.5 crore compute jobs (a complex task or simulation assigned to a supercomputer) and contributed to over 1,990 research publications, as of September 2026.
To further expand the skilled user base, the Mission has developed a range of training and learning initiatives:
HPC and Deep Learning Awareness Programmes:
Workshops are conducted across India with NSM institutions to introduce students, researchers and faculty to High-Performance Computing (HPC) and Deep Learning (DL).
Hackathons and Bootcamps:
HPC and DL hackathons and bootcamps provide hands-on experience and encourage problem-solving in HPC, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI.
Faculty Development and Quality Improvement Programmes:
Faculty, including teachers from non-computer science disciplines, are trained in HPC, AI, Machine Learning (ML) and DL in collaboration with the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE).
EduHPC Workshop:
An annual workshop provides comprehensive training in HPC to faculty from institutions across India.
High-Performance Scientific Computing Course:
A structured course on the SWAYAM platform, under the National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL), helps learners build a strong foundation in HPC.
HPC Shiksha Portal:
The portal provides access to HPC resources, recorded lectures and learning materials, enabling students and teachers to gain practical experience.
NSM Users Forum:
The forum provides a platform for users across NSM sites to discuss technical issues, resolve queries and share knowledge and best practices.
National Knowledge Network (NKN)
The NKN serves as the backbone of India’s supercomputing ecosystem under the National Supercomputing Mission. It connects supercomputing facilities across academic and research institutions through a high-speed national network. This enables researchers and institutions to access advanced computing resources and collaborate across geographical boundaries. The network strengthens the sharing of computational resources, research capabilities and scientific knowledge. Through this connected infrastructure, the Mission is expanding access to High-Performance Computing across India.
These initiatives are expanding HPC skills beyond specialised computing institutions and building a broader workforce equipped to use advanced computing.
Way Forward
India’s supercomputing ecosystem is set to grow significantly by expanding computing capacity, developing more advanced technologies within the country, and making high-performance computing (HPC) more accessible to researchers, academia and industry. The focus of the mission will be on building faster, energy-efficient and reliable systems, strengthening Indian hardware and software capabilities, and developing skilled professionals. Greater integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and HPC will help address important challenges in areas such as weather and climate, healthcare, agriculture, energy, drug discovery, engineering and scientific research. By bringing together government, academia, industry, startups and research institutions, India can turn advanced computing into practical solutions, drive innovation and economic growth, and build a secure, sustainable and self-reliant supercomputing ecosystem.
